section_summary: This section covers British and American commercial credits to Japan, Japanese bond sales, and government budgets from 1937 to 1941. It also contains correspondence about a claim to Japanese government bonds, military attaché reports on Japanese finance, and older file references concerning Japanese loans.

people.name: Herschel V. Johnson
people.role: American chargé d’affaires ad interim in London

people.name: Bennett E. Siegelstein
people.role: Counselor at law representing the estate administrator

people.name: Oliver D. Hovey
people.role: Deceased person whose estate claimed Japanese bonds

people.name: N. Bernard Cohen
people.role: Petitioner seeking discovery concerning Japanese bonds

people.name: F. J. Hellman
people.role: Vice president, Wells Fargo Bank and Union Trust Company

people.name: Pierre Jaudel
people.role: Lawyer and author of an article on Tokyo bonds

people.name: Norman Armour
people.role: American chargé d’affaires ad interim in Paris

subfiles.title: British credits to Japan, concluding page
subfiles.about: British banks and firms appear to be reducing sterling credits available to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Johnson reports indications of declining British credit facilities.

subfiles.title: Japan (Credits), Hansard excerpt
subfiles.about: A parliamentary question concerns London financing of Japanese purchases of Australian wool.
subfiles.summary: Simon says he has no reason to believe London institutions are increasing credits to Japan.

subfiles.title: British Credits to Japan
subfiles.about: The embassy forwards a parliamentary exchange and assesses Japan’s sterling credit facilities.
subfiles.summary: Johnson forwards Hansard and reports indications that British banks and firms are further reducing credit facilities for Japan.

subfiles.title: Japan (Credits), Hansard excerpt
subfiles.about: A question asks whether London banks finance Japanese commodity purchases.
subfiles.summary: Simon denies evidence of increasing London credits to Japan.

subfiles.title: Possible Swiss credit to Japan
subfiles.about: The note points to a report on Uebersee-Handel A.G. and possible Swiss credit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Swiss report on a possible credit.

subfiles.title: Japanese government bonds issued in May 1939
subfiles.about: The note records ¥214 million in May bond issues and opposition to compulsory sales.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a report on May bond issues.

subfiles.title: Estate of Oliver D. Hovey
subfiles.about: Counsel asks the Department to reconsider its position after dismissal of discovery proceedings against the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: Siegelstein requests renewed consideration of the estate’s claim.

subfiles.title: Request for the Surrogate’s Court decision
subfiles.about: The Department asks for an authoritative copy of the court decision.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth says the Department will review the decision if supplied.

subfiles.title: Court order enclosed
subfiles.about: Siegelstein submits a certified court order concerning the estate’s claim.
subfiles.summary: Counsel encloses a certified order and awaits a reply.

subfiles.title: Department position on Hovey bond claim
subfiles.about: The Department declines to present the estate’s Japanese bond claim.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth explains that the submitted dismissal order is not the court’s written decision and gives no support for the claimed entitlement to the bonds. The Department therefore maintains its refusal to submit the claim to Japan.

subfiles.title: Commercial Credits to Japan
subfiles.about: A banker asks about continuing secured commercial credits for exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hellman describes short term credits to Japanese banks secured by dollar bonds. Department officers cite exchange controls and urge consideration of broader American interests, while noting that no law bars the credits.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmission of credits memorandum
subfiles.to: American chargé d’affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department sends its conversation with Hellman for confidential information.
subfiles.summary: Confidential cover instruction transmitting the September 18 memorandum.

subfiles.title: Government finance in July 1939
subfiles.about: The note points to a July report on Japanese government finance.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch 4108.

subfiles.title: Government Finance
subfiles.about: The excerpt reviews July bond issues and proposed tax reform.
subfiles.summary: The Finance Ministry issued ¥400 million in China Incident bonds. Reports describe better public absorption of bonds and a proposed income tax overhaul expected to raise roughly ¥500 million annually.

subfiles.title: Japanese budget and defense expenditure figures
subfiles.about: The note points to a table of Japan’s 1938–39 budget and defense spending.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a memorandum using military intelligence figures.

subfiles.title: Proposed cotton sale on credit to Japan
subfiles.about: Proffitt asks whether a Brooklyn company may sell goods on credit to the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: Green says the Department does not favor credit sales to Japan and suggests an in-person discussion.

subfiles.title: Charge slip
subfiles.about: A file charge slip records internal handling of the enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Internal file routing record.

subfiles.title: Financial affairs in November 1939
subfiles.about: The note points to a November report on Japanese financial affairs.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch 4377.

subfiles.title: Government Finance, November 1939
subfiles.about: The excerpt covers November bond sales, bank notes, and war financing.
subfiles.summary: A ¥400 million bond issue met weaker demand than earlier in the year. The report describes limits on corporate finance, a rising Bank of Japan note issue, and Finance Minister Aoki’s assertion that war spending had been financed domestically.

subfiles.title: Japanese finance ministry economy program
subfiles.about: The excerpt lists proposed savings and deferred projects in Japanese government accounts.
subfiles.summary: A partial report tabulates cuts and notes press concern over secrecy.

subfiles.title: Note on 1938–39 Japanese budget estimates
subfiles.about: The memorandum comments on limited information about Japan’s 1938–39 budget.
subfiles.summary: It cautions that estimates exclude China Incident spending.

subfiles.title: 1938–39 Budget: Preliminary Decisions
subfiles.about: The report assesses preliminary Japanese budget estimates and expected China war costs.
subfiles.summary: The report describes projected army and navy allocations, postponed civilian projects, and the need for bonds and taxes. It stresses that China operations require separate, substantial appropriations.

subfiles.title: Finance: Japanese popular opinion
subfiles.doc_type: military attaché report with press clipping
subfiles.about: The report forwards an article defending Japan’s economic strength.
subfiles.summary: Shigeyoshi Hijikata disputes Nathaniel Peffer’s prediction of economic failure, arguing that national income, savings, industrial capacity, and social endurance can sustain the China campaign. The attaché identifies the article as a Japanese view of current conditions.

subfiles.title: Employment of Gold Reserve
subfiles.about: Japan plans to use ¥300 million of Bank of Japan gold reserves to finance raw materials for exports.
subfiles.summary: The report explains the revolving foreign exchange fund, its intended support for export production, and official assurances about the yen. Creswell notes that success depends on how quickly imported materials can be processed and sold abroad.

subfiles.title: Budget for Fiscal Year 1939–1940
subfiles.about: The report analyzes draft regular budget estimates for 1939–40.
subfiles.summary: Creswell gives ministry allocations, revenue sources, and comparisons with the previous budget. The regular budget excludes China Incident appropriations, whose eventual scale is expected to be large; he discusses bonds, taxation, and war related increases across ministries.

subfiles.title: Appropriations for Fiscal Year 1939–1940
subfiles.about: The report details Japan’s enacted regular, supplementary, and China Incident budgets.
subfiles.summary: The report lists departmental appropriations and revenue, including major bond financing. It calculates a combined budget of about ¥9.41 billion, discusses military and special accounts, and notes authority for additional military contracts outside the budget.

subfiles.title: Appropriations for Fiscal Year 1940–1941
subfiles.about: The report reviews preliminary estimates for Japan’s 1940–41 budget.
subfiles.summary: Press figures suggest a budget above ¥10 billion, including China Incident accounts. Creswell presents incomplete ministry and revenue estimates and expects substantial further bond issues despite possible tax changes.

subfiles.title: South Manchurian Railway domestic loan
subfiles.about: The note points to a proposed domestic loan for South Manchurian Railway industrial development.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Commerce Department letter 894.51/338.

subfiles.title: Toho Electric Power bond issue
subfiles.about: The note points to a memorandum on the approaching maturity of a Toho Electric Power bond issue.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to memorandum 894.51/339.

subfiles.title: City of Tokyo prewar bond litigation
subfiles.about: The note points to a despatch enclosing Pierre Jaudel’s article on Tokyo bond litigation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch 1078.

subfiles.title: Le procès « Ville de Tokio »
subfiles.about: Jaudel explains a dispute over whether Tokyo’s prewar French bonds are payable in gold francs.
subfiles.summary: The article sets out the city’s and bondholders’ competing readings of the bond terms before a final French court ruling.

subfiles.title: Prewar Tokyo bonds and gold payments
subfiles.about: Armour forwards Jaudel’s article and notes a separate Costa Rican gold franc bond decision.
subfiles.summary: The despatch identifies the pending Tokyo bond litigation and encloses the article. It also reports Costa Rica’s decision to honor a court ruling requiring gold franc payments on its 1911 loan.

subfiles.title: Decision in 1912 City of Tokyo loan case
subfiles.about: The note points to a French Supreme Court decision concerning the City of Tokyo’s 1912 five percent loan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to the court decision report.
